uniform_prefix.reason: only 1 usable point(s); a crossover needs at least 2

hot_prefix_skew.predicted: prefix_aware LOSES unless affinity is blended with load: one very hot prefix sends a disproportionate share of traffic to whichever replica owns it. §10 calls this the most likely place for a genuinely bad result, and therefore the most valuable one to measure.

system_prompt_sharing.predicted: prefix_aware SHOULD beat B5 here: several distinct prefixes, so affinity carries real information and does not collapse onto one replica.

uniform_prefix.predicted: B5 WINS. Every request shares the same prefix, so every replica caches it after warmup and prefix awareness degenerates to 'pick any replica'. This is the naive mental model of prefix caching and the case where the clever router is worth nothing.

verdicts: uniform_prefix: PREDICTION HELD (§10.2). prefix_aware does not beat B5 at any load tested (1 loss(es), 0 tie(s)) — as predicted before the run.
hot_prefix_skew: PREDICTION HELD (§10.7). prefix_aware does not beat B5 at any load tested (2 loss(es), 0 tie(s)) — as predicted before the run.

system_prompt_sharing: prefix_aware beats B5 at [8.0] and loses at [0.5] req/s. never ahead: the advantage is -0.008333 at the lowest x (0.5). There is no crossover to report because there was no lead to lose.
